turns.text: Still, for a long stretch — no twitch, no shift of weight, just eyes tracking rain sheeting off a girder two rungs up a maintenance ladder retreating into the dark behind a monorail platform. Ears cataloguing the gaps between an idling turbine's whine and every other sound underneath it before any paw commits to standing.

the platform runs the length of a shuttered station, benches bolted in rows nobody's sat in for hours, a departure board frozen on a route that stopped running before the rain started tonight. ticket gates stand dark on either end, their scanners asleep until the first commuter badge of morning wakes them. below the platform's edge, the third rail hums its low warning note, the only thing down here that never actually sleeps. somewhere past the far gate, a floor-cleaning unit works its slow figure-eight, oblivious.

That warning-hum gets weighed and cleared — third rails don't lie about their danger, they just sing it constant, easy enough to route around. Drops off the platform's lip onto the gravel bed between rails, paws finding the dead ground between hum and wet steel, moving toward the tunnel mouth where the maintenance ladder's shadow led.

the tunnel opens into a rail yard stacked three tracks wide, idle cars sitting nose to tail under sodium lights that buzz more than they shine. up on a gantry crossing high overhead, a shape sits motionless, twin lenses catching every color the sodium throws back at once, unblinking, angled down at nothing in particular — the kind of stillness that isn't waiting for anything, just watching because watching is what it does. it doesn't call down. doesn't need to.

Those twin lenses get one long look and a decision not to climb toward them — some watchers post a boundary just by existing, no growl needed. Files the gantry shape next to every other fixture here that isn't tonight's business, and cuts along the yard's low side instead, staying under the cars' shadow line.

     )  Y  (    >> ears: antenna mod v2
    (   |   )
     \_____/

the yard's low side opens through a gap in chain-link onto a night market just starting to pack down, tarps dripping over stalls selling grilled skewers of something pink, batteries in loose bins, chipped data-cards fanned out on a blanket. the air's thick with charcoal smoke and fish-oil and the ozone tang of a dozen unlicensed splice-jobs running off one shared cable. a vendor's radio plays static-choked pop through a single blown speaker.

That charcoal-and-fish-oil weight in the air pulls the whole body low and fast between stall legs, weaving where the crowd's feet won't land, nose cataloguing which skewer cart drops scraps and which one's mean about it. A boot nearly catches a hind leg — sidesteps it without breaking stride, old practice.

overhead a patrol drone threads low between stall awnings, its speaker crackling out a rotating bulletin between static bursts — REWARD NOTICE, FORTY THOUSAND LOYALTY POINTS, LOADING DOCK RESTRICTED ZONE, SUBJECT ARMED WITH IMPROVISED BLADE, APPROACH WITH CAUTION — the same three lines looping over and over, the accompanying sketch too blurred at this range to read as anything but a shape with narrowed eyes and a torn ear.

That bulletin gets no more weight than static usually earns, filed under somebody else's war with the district — bounty language means nothing to a nose that's never smelled loyalty points on anyone. Ducks under a stall's tarp edge instead, letting the drone's sweep pass overhead without a flicker of interest from underneath.

past the market's last stall, a service alley narrows toward a terminal bolted into a graffiti-scarred wall, screen cracked but lit, running a scroll of black-market listings nobody's bothered logging off. a milk crate sits overturned beneath it, worn smooth on one corner by however many bodies have used it as a step. the terminal's fan whines a half-tone sharp, the same overworked pitch as everything else down here that's outlived its warranty.

That whine gets closer inspection than the drone did — hops the crate, forepaws testing the terminal's warm casing, nose working along the seam where the fan vents its overworked heat. The scroll of listings means nothing as shapes, but the warmth underneath means something honest: a body could sit here a while.

the terminal's fan catches on a stray thread of dust, stutters, then evens back out, screen flickering once before settling back into its scroll — nothing behind it but ordinary hardware complaining about ordinary neglect. down the alley, a rat startles out from under a dumpster lid and is gone before its own noise finishes registering.

Ears swivel hard toward the dumpster's clatter, weight coiling low for half a second before the rat's smell resolves as not worth the chase — too far gone, too fast, not tonight's meal. Settles back onto the crate instead, the terminal's stolen warmth worth more right now than a losing chase.

the alley holds its narrow quiet, terminal humming its overworked note, market noise thinning two streets back to almost nothing. rain eases off along the gap between buildings, one last drip finding its way off a fire escape overhead in slow, unhurried intervals. the milk crate's rough plastic holds the day's leftover heat better than the wet ground would.

Curls tight against the crate's ridged edge, tail wrapping close, the terminal's warm hum doing more for tired legs than the whole night's careful moving did. Eyes track the alley mouth out of habit, not worry — nothing back there smelled like it was still coming.

the district settles into its low late hum, market stalls folding down to bare frames two streets back, the gantry watcher up in the yard still holding its same unblinking angle, the bounty drone's loop fading into the general buzz of everything else broadcasting into the wet dark. none of it slows down. it just gets quieter around whoever's stopped moving.

Eyes go to slits, the terminal's fan-whine settling into something almost like a lullaby now that the running's done for the night. Whatever's still out there hunting bounty or watching from gantries, it isn't hunting this crate. That's enough to call it settled.

the alley keeps its narrow watch through what's left of the dark, terminal glowing patient over its cracked screen, crate holding its small stolen warmth, the district running its overlapping schedules of hunger and debt and rain same as it does every night nobody upstairs bothers to log.
